minutes.headline: Committee ratified cafeteria and custodial contracts and moved Turkey Hill assessment to top of capital priorities.
minutes.summary: The committee heard from the new facilities director, ratified two three-year union agreements with the town manager voting, and approved related salary line-item transfers. It approved the 2024 eighth-grade DC trip, named LEA negotiators, adopted the bullying plan and a resignation policy, and re-ranked its capital priorities. A long executive session took up the middle of the evening.

public_comment.topic: Congratulated everyone on Homecoming and the football win, and noted the upcoming playoff game.
Chair asked for public comment at the end; none offered.

what_happened.line: The School Committee ratified three-year contracts for cafeteria workers and custodians by roll call, with the town manager voting yes.
The committee approved a transfer from the school salary reserve to custodial staffing accounts, which uses up that reserve.
It approved two routine fall transfers for teacher and paraprofessional salary lines.
It re-ranked its capital priorities, changing the Turkey Hill item to assessment and schematic design with a value subject to confirmation.
Turf field design moved to seventh priority on a 4-1 vote, behind driveway and playground design.

why_it_matters: The custodial contract's three-year cost lands on the local budget, while the cafeteria contract is paid from a revolving account, so only one of the two touches the tax-funded school budget.
The capital priority order and the Turkey Hill request shape what the town may be asked to fund later, and the committee has not yet set the final number.
watch_next: Capital planning returns at the next meeting to finalize the number, and a budget priorities discussion has been requested for a future meeting.
The chair is to compile a special town meeting presentation on the primary school air conditioning article.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nearly every vote and outcome, and most figure differences are caption garbling of the same amounts. The one substantive split is the capital-priority votes: ours records a flip of items, the official minutes record approval of items 1-6, and neither record has the other.
